parsed_answer.content:
A Data Lake is a centralized repository designed to store vast amounts of raw data in its native format—structured, semi-structured, or unstructured—until it is needed. It operates on the principle of 'schema-on-read,' where data is ingested without transformation, offloading the complexity of processing to the consumer. While powerful for exploratory analysis and machine learning, Data Lakes often devolve into 'Data Swamps' due to a lack of governance, ownership, and discoverability, creating a monolithic bottleneck where a central data engineering team becomes the gatekeeper for all data requests.

Data Mesh is a socio-technical paradigm shift that moves away from this monolithic, centralized architecture toward a decentralized, domain-oriented approach. Instead of treating data as a byproduct of applications to be dumped into a lake, Data Mesh treats data as a 'product.' Each business domain (e.g., Inventory, Billing, User Profile) owns its data lifecycle, from ingestion to serving. This architecture relies on four pillars: Domain Ownership, Data as a Product, Self-serve Data Infrastructure as a Platform, and Federated Computational Governance. By distributing responsibility, Data Mesh solves the scaling bottlenecks of Data Lakes, allowing organizations to treat data pipelines with the same rigor as microservices.

items: Data Lake internals rely on object storage (S3, GCS) and compute engines (Spark, Trino) that decouple storage from compute, but they fail to decouple the organizational bottleneck of the central data team.

Data Mesh leverages 'Data Products' which are essentially encapsulated units of data, metadata, and code (often exposed via GraphQL or high-performance SQL interfaces) that adhere to global interoperability standards defined by the federated governance group.

In a Data Mesh, the 'Self-serve Data Platform' is a critical engineering layer that provides the underlying infrastructure (CI/CD, monitoring, schema registry) so that domain teams don't have to reinvent the wheel for every data product.

parsed_answer.content: The most common trap for organizations moving to Data Mesh is ignoring the 'socio' part of 'socio-technical.' You cannot simply re-architect your storage; you must re-architect your team structure. If your domain teams lack the engineering maturity to own their data pipelines, the Mesh will fail. Always start by identifying your 'Domain Bounded Contexts'—if you haven't mastered Domain-Driven Design (DDD), you aren't ready for a Data Mesh.

title: Explain what a "Data Mesh" is compared to a "Data Lake".
